Free public tool

AI assistants are becoming a front door. The facts they repeat need inspection.

GEO Audit Studio helps social-impact organizations test whether AI tools can find, understand, cite, and accurately represent their public websites. It gives staff a structured audit brief, a one-screen executive result, prompt tests, and a practical action plan without requiring a paid platform or private analytics access.

For Nonprofit Staff

Nonprofit communications and development teams need to know what AI assistants say when a donor, journalist, partner, or board member asks about their organization. A weak website can cause AI tools to miss current programs, confuse eligibility, repeat stale leadership, cite old directories, or recommend better-described peer organizations.

The nonprofit preset focuses on donor-facing questions: what the organization does, who it serves, what evidence supports its impact claims, how someone can give or engage, and which source-of-truth pages need to be clearer.

For Foundation Staff

Foundations have a different risk. If AI assistants misstate funding priorities, geography, grant size, exclusions, deadlines, or application routes, grantseekers waste time and program staff absorb avoidable noise. Bad AI summaries can also make a funder look inconsistent when the real problem is scattered public guidance.

The funder preset tests whether AI tools describe the foundation's actual funding priorities accurately to grantseekers. It pushes the audit toward eligibility, exclusions, current programs, source documents, and the applicant questions most likely to create confusion.

Why I Built It

I build free tools for social-impact teams because bad information wastes scarce money, staff time, attention, and trust. GEO Audit Studio is meant to improve resource allocation: donors should find organizations that actually match their intent, nonprofits should not lose visibility because their facts are hard to parse, and grantseekers should not chase foundations based on inaccurate AI summaries.

The tool is deliberately transparent. It does not claim to know private AI rankings. It gives teams a repeatable way to test what public AI systems retrieve, what they cite, what they get wrong, and what website owners can fix first.
